mainTopic: Extra verses that teach new laws (ויקרא ז:יט), and רבי יוחנן's rule that מלקות apply only to normal eating or benefit, with אביי's exception for כלאי הכרם.
overview: This amud opens at the end of a challenge about the צירעה, which brings six sets of מלקות because many verses forbid it. רב אשי answers with a rule: whenever a verse can teach something new, we learn it that way and do not read it as just another לאו. The גמרא applies this rule to ויקרא ז:יט. The first half includes עצים and לבונה, and the second half includes the אימורין. The second half is not a repeat of the next verse, because that verse deals with a טמא person (כרת) and ours deals with טמא meat (a לאו). Next, רבי יוחנן teaches that מלקות are given only for using a forbidden item in its normal way. One version speaks of eating, and another speaks of benefit, with the examples of raw חלב and fat placed on a wound. רבי זירא tries to prove this from a משנה about ערלה juices, and אביי rejects the proof. אביי then rules that for כלאי הכרם there are מלקות even for unusual benefit, because 'eating' is not written about them. The גמרא begins a challenge to him from איסי בן יהודה's sources for בשר בחלב, and the challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The hornet case: many lashes for one act of eating
steps.stepSummary: The challenge ends with the case of a צירעה, for which one receives six sets of מלקות. This shows that the Torah does repeat prohibitions just to add more לאוין.
steps.simpleTranslation: [One who eats] a hornet is flogged six times!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of a challenge that began on the previous amud. The challenger points to a צירעה: eating it brings six sets of lashes, because several different verses forbid it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenger's point is that the Torah sometimes stacks extra לאוין on one item just to increase the punishment. If so, an extra 'לא יאכל' may only add another לאו. It would not prove a new law.

keyTerms.meaning: A hornet. It is both a creeping and a flying insect, so many prohibitions apply to it.
He receives lashes (מלקות).
Six, meaning six separate sets of lashes.

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new ruling standing on its own. It is the end of a challenge from the previous text, and it is used to argue that extra verses may only add punishment.

phrases.english: A hornet — he is flogged six [times]!
phrases.notes: The end of a ברייתא listing insects that bring multiple sets of lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge that began on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that an extra 'לא יאכל' must teach a new law.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The צירעה case shows the Torah can repeat לאוין only to add lashes, so an extra phrase may teach no new law.

steps.title: The rule: if a verse can teach something new, we use it that way
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that whenever a verse can be expounded for a new law, we expound it. We do not treat it as just an extra לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Wherever it is possible to expound, we expound, and we do not read [the verse] as extra prohibitions.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the hornet challenge with a general rule. Extra לאוין are only the fallback, used when no new law can be learned from the verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The צירעה verses each get counted as a לאו because there is nothing else to learn from them. When a verse can teach a new law, that reading wins over 'just another לאו'. This rule sets up the rest of this passage, where the גמרא looks for what each part of the verse teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: To expound; to learn a new law from the verse.
We expound it.
We establish or read [the verse] as.
Extra negative commandments.

steps.whatToRemember: A rule of Torah reading: the Torah's extra words teach new laws whenever possible. Only when nothing new can be learned do we count them as additional לאוין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle explains why the גמרא in the next steps works hard to find a new teaching in each half of the verse.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Anywhere it is possible to expound — we expound,
and we do not establish it as extra negative commandments.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא לְמִדְרַשׁ — דָּרְשִׁינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the צירעה case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: General interpretive principle that limits the challenger's case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Extra verses might only add more לאוין, as with the צירעה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Extra לאוין are only a last resort. When a new law can be learned, we learn it.

steps.title: Why do we need the first half of the verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the first half of ויקרא ז:יט, 'flesh that touches anything impure shall not be eaten', teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the flesh that touches anything impure shall not be eaten': why do I need the beginning of it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now applies the rule it just stated to a specific verse. It asks what new law the first half of the verse teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following רב אשי's rule, we should not read this phrase as merely another לאו. So the גמרא looks for a new teaching hidden in it.

keyTerms.meaning: Its beginning; the first half of the verse.
Why do I need it?
Ritually impure.

phrases.aramaic: ״וְהַבָּשָׂר אֲשֶׁר יִגַּע בְּכׇל טָמֵא לֹא יֵאָכֵל״
phrases.english: 'And the flesh that touches anything impure shall not be eaten'
why do I need its beginning?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule from step 2 to a specific verse.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new law the first half of ויקרא ז:יט teaches.

steps.title: It includes wood and frankincense
steps.stepSummary: The first half of the verse teaches that עצים and לבונה, though not food, can also become טמא like food.
steps.simpleTranslation: To include wood and frankincense.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the first half of the verse includes the wood of the altar and the frankincense in the laws of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally only food can receive טומאת אוכלין. The extra words widen the category to holy items of the מקדש that are not eaten. So the verse teaches a real new law, not just an extra לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: To include.
Wood, meaning the wood used on the altar.
Frankincense.

phrases.english: To include wood and frankincense.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first half of the verse includes עצים and לבונה as able to become טמא.

steps.title: Why do we need the second half of the verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the end of the verse, 'and the flesh, every pure person may eat flesh', teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the flesh, every pure person may eat flesh': why do I need the end of it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second half of the same verse and asks the same question: what new law does it teach?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase seems to just repeat that pure people may eat the meat. Following the rule, the גמרא assumes it must hold a new teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Its end; the second half of the verse.
Ritually pure.

phrases.english: 'And the flesh, every pure one may eat flesh'
why do I need its end?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel question about the other half of the verse.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new law the second half of ויקרא ז:יט teaches.

steps.title: It includes the altar portions
steps.stepSummary: The end of the verse includes the אימורין, the parts burned on the altar. They also count as 'meat' for טומאה, and eating them when they are טמא is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: To include the sacrificial parts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the end of the verse includes the אימורין. If they become טמא, even a pure person may not eat them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think the altar parts are not 'meat for eating', since they go to the מזבח. The verse includes them, so a pure person who eats טמא אימורין violates this לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: The portions of a קרבן burned on the altar, such as the fats.

phrases.english: To include the sacrificial parts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second half includes the אימורין in the prohibition of eating טמא meat.

steps.title: But the altar portions are already learned from another verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges that the אימורין are already included by a ברייתא on the next verse (ויקרא ז:כ), so this verse should not be needed for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sacrificial parts are derived from there, as it was taught: 'And the soul that eats flesh from the peace-offering which is to ה׳' — to include the sacrificial parts!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer. A ברייתא already learns the אימורין from the words 'אשר לה׳' in the next verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the אימורין are already included elsewhere, then using the end of ז:יט for them would be a repeat. That would bring back the problem of an extra verse with no new teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: It is derived from there, meaning from another source.
The peace-offering.
Which is to ה׳. These words include the parts that go to the altar.

phrases.english: The sacrificial parts are derived from there,
as it was taught:
'And the soul that eats flesh
from the peace-offering which is to ה׳'
— to include the sacrificial parts!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the end of ז:יט is needed to include the אימורין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא already includes the אימורין from ז:כ, so the derivation in step 6 is a repeat.

steps.title: Impure person versus impure meat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the two verses cover different cases. The ברייתא's verse deals with an impure person eating, which carries כרת. Our verse deals with impure meat eaten by a pure person, which carries a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is impurity of the body, with כרת. Here it is impurity of the meat, with a לאו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by showing the two verses teach two different laws about the אימורין, so neither one is extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ויקרא ז:כ includes the אימורין when a טמא person eats them; the punishment is כרת. ויקרא ז:יט includes the אימורין when the meat itself is טמא and the person is pure; the punishment is a לאו. Both derivations stand, which fits רב אשי's rule that verses teach new laws.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity of the body: the person eating is טמא.
Impurity of the meat: the food itself is טמא.
Spiritual cutting off, a heavenly punishment.
A negative commandment, punishable by lashes.

steps.whatToRemember: The אימורין appear in two prohibitions. A טמא person eating them gets כרת (ז:כ). A pure person eating טמא אימורין violates a לאו (ז:יט).
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'impure person' and 'impure meat'. They are two different prohibitions with two different punishments, and each comes from its own verse.

phrases.english: There, impurity of the body — with karet,
here, impurity of the flesh — with a negative commandment.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם טוּמְאַת הַגּוּף — בְּכָרֵת, הָכָא טוּמְאַת בָּשָׂר — בְּלָאו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: each verse addresses a different kind of טומאה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both verses seem to teach the same inclusion of the אימורין.
steps.terutzMaskana: ז:כ covers a טמא person (כרת). ז:יט covers טמא meat eaten by a pure person (לאו).

steps.title: Lashes only for eating in the normal way
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו quotes רבי יוחנן: for all Torah prohibitions, מלקות are given only when the item is eaten in its normal manner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: For every prohibition in the Torah, a person gets lashes only if he eats the forbidden thing the way people normally eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new general rule from רבי יוחנן about when a person gets מלקות for eating forbidden food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule sets a condition on punishment. It is not enough that the forbidden item went into your mouth. It has to be eaten in the normal way that food like it is eaten. Anything unusual does not earn מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Prohibitions written in the Torah
They give lashes (מלקות)
The normal way of eating them

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle (שלא כדרך אכילתן) appears all over שס and in practical הלכה about forbidden foods.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
All prohibitions that are in the Torah
one is not given lashes for them
except in their normal manner of eating.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After discussing what is forbidden to eat or to benefit from, the גמרא brings a related rule about when punishment applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מלקות for Torah food prohibitions apply only when the item is eaten in its normal manner.

steps.title: What case does this rule exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which case רבי יוחנן's rule is meant to leave out.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this rule coming to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a concrete example of eating that does not count as 'the normal way.' This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A general rule needs a practical case to show what it means. The question asks which unusual kind of eating does not get מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude what? (What case is being left out?)

phrases.english: To exclude what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical application of the rule in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which specific case is left out by the requirement of דרך אכילתן.

steps.title: Eating raw fat is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי answers that the rule excludes someone who eats raw חלב. He is exempt from מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי said: It excludes a person who ate raw forbidden fat. He is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי gives the example: eating raw חלב is not the normal way to eat it, so there are no מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חלב (forbidden fat) is normally eaten cooked or melted. Eating it raw is unusual, so even though the person ate a forbidden item, he does not get lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: Raw forbidden fat
Exempt (from punishment)

steps.confusionAlert: פטור here means he gets no מלקות. It does not mean that eating raw חלב is permitted.

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi said:
To exclude a case where one ate raw forbidden fat,
that he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי לְמַעוֹטֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule excludes eating raw חלב, which is not a normal way of eating, so there are no מלקות.

steps.title: Second version: lashes only for normal benefit
steps.stepSummary: Some report רבי יוחנן's rule differently: for prohibitions on benefit, מלקות apply only when one benefits in the normal manner.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say this is what רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: For every prohibition in the Torah, a person gets lashes only if he benefits from the forbidden thing in the normal way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רבי יוחנן's statement. In this version the rule is about benefit instead of eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the last words change: 'דרך הנאתן' (normal way of benefit) instead of 'דרך אכילתן' (normal way of eating). This moves the rule to items that are forbidden even to benefit from. Unusual kinds of benefit do not get מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: The normal way of benefiting from them

phrases.english: Some say:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
All prohibitions that are in the Torah
one is not given lashes for them
except in their normal manner of benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the statement in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For prohibitions on benefit, מלקות apply only to benefit taken in the normal manner.

steps.title: What does the second version exclude?
steps.stepSummary: Again the גמרא asks which case this version of the rule leaves out.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this rule coming to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question as before, now about the 'benefit' version. This sets up a new example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule now covers benefit, so the excluded case will be an unusual kind of benefit, not just an unusual kind of eating.

phrases.english: To exclude what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical application of the version in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case is left out by the requirement of דרך הנאתן.

steps.title: Putting forbidden fat on a wound is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי says it excludes placing fat of a שור הנסקל on a wound, and all the more so eating raw fat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי said: It excludes a person who put the fat of an ox that is to be stoned on his wound. He is exempt. And all the more so, a person who eats raw fat is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי gives an example of unusual benefit: using forbidden fat as a bandage for a wound. He adds that eating raw fat is exempt even more clearly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שור הנסקל is forbidden for any benefit. Still, putting its fat on a wound is not the usual way people use fat, so there are no מלקות. Raw fat is exempt 'all the more so' because eating it raw is not a normal way of benefiting from fat either.

keyTerms.meaning: An ox sentenced to stoning (forbidden for any benefit)
His wound
All the more so

steps.confusionAlert: In this version, raw fat is still exempt. The 'benefit' version does not argue on the raw-fat ruling. It includes it with a כל שכן.

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi said:
To exclude a case where one placed
the fat of an ox that is to be stoned
on top of his wound,
that he is exempt.
And all the more so one who eats raw fat,
that he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי לְמַעוֹטֵי שֶׁאִם הִנִּיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Placing fat of a שור הנסקל on a wound is unusual benefit and gets no מלקות. Eating raw fat is exempt all the more so.

steps.title: Another tradition confirms the benefit version
steps.stepSummary: Through another chain of rabbis, רבי יוחנן is quoted ruling that fat of a שור הנסקל placed on a wound is exempt, because of the דרך הנאתן rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רב אחא בר עויא said in the name of רב אסי, in the name of רבי יוחנן: If someone put the fat of an ox that is to be stoned on his wound, he is exempt. This is because for every prohibition in the Torah, a person gets lashes only if he benefits in the normal way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report of רבי יוחנן's teaching. It backs up the 'benefit' version and the wound example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This tradition comes through a different chain (רב אחא בר עויא, from רב אסי). It states both the wound case and the reason, דרך הנאתן. That supports the second version of רבי יוחנן's words.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (another tradition says the same)
Because

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Rav Aḥa bar Avya said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: that Rav Asi said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
If one placed fat of an ox that is to be stoned
on top of his wound, he is exempt,
because all prohibitions that are in the Torah,
one is not given lashes for them
except in their normal manner of benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the version and example given in steps 12 and 14.
steps.raayaObject: The 'דרך הנאתן' version of רבי יוחנן's rule and the wound example.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A separate tradition from רב אחא בר עויא in the name of רב אסי, quoting רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Support from the law of ערלה juices
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא shows that a משנה already teaches this rule: for ערלה, מלקות apply only to juice from olives and grapes, because other fruits are not normally used for juice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: We also learned this in a משנה: A person gets the forty lashes for ערלה only for what comes out of olives and grapes. But for juice from mulberries, figs, and pomegranates, he does not. What is the reason? Isn't it because he is not using them in their normal way?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא brings a משנה that shows the same idea. Juice from fruits that people don't normally squeeze does not bring מלקות, even when it is ערלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Olive oil and wine are normal ways to use olives and grapes, so drinking ערלה oil or wine brings מלקות. Mulberries, figs, and pomegranates are normally eaten, not squeezed. So drinking their juice is not the normal way and brings no lashes. The question 'מאי טעמא' is a rhetorical question that pulls the principle out of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it (in a משנה)
Receive the forty lashes
Fruit of a tree in its first three years, forbidden to eat and to benefit from
What comes out (the juice or liquid)
Mulberries

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's rule: there are no מלקות for a Torah prohibition unless the item is used in its normal way. One version says eating (raw fat is exempt). The other says benefit (fat on a wound is exempt, and raw fat all the more so). רבי זירא tries to support the rule from a משנה about ערלה juices, but the next step shows that אביי rejects this proof.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
We too have also learned this:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין סוֹפְגִין אֶת הָאַרְבָּעִים מִשּׁוּם עׇרְלָה,
phrases.english: One does not receive the forty lashes on account of ערלה
except for what comes out
from olives and from grapes alone.
But from mulberries, figs, and pomegranates, not.
What is the reason?
Is it not because he is not consuming them
in their normal manner of benefit?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה that supports רבי יוחנן's principle.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's principle that מלקות apply only to normal use of the forbidden item.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה ruling that ערלה juice brings מלקות only from olives and grapes, not from mulberries, figs, or pomegranates.

steps.title: אביי rejects the proof from the juice משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that the ערלה juice משנה does not prove the דרך הנאתן rule. Juice from fruits other than olives and grapes may be exempt simply because it is mere 'sweat,' not real fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: It would be fine if the משנה had taught us about the fruit itself, where the person is not using it the normal way. But here, the juice may be exempt simply because it is just 'sweat' coming out of the fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects רבי זירא's proof from Step 16. He offers a different reason why the juice of other fruits does not bring מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא said the juice of other fruits is exempt because squeezing them is not their normal use. אביי says there is another possible reason: that liquid is just 'sweat,' moisture that is not considered part of the fruit at all. So the משנה does not have to be about 'normal use.' The proof would only work if the משנה had been talking about the actual fruit eaten in an unusual way.

keyTerms.meaning: It would make sense / granted (if the case were different)
The fruit itself
Well / it would work fine
Sweat / moisture, liquid not considered part of the fruit itself

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the juice is permitted for normal reasons. He is saying the reason it carries no מלקות may have nothing to do with 'normal use.' It may simply be that this liquid does not count as the fruit.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Granted, if it had taught us about the fruit itself,

steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The juice exemption can be explained by its being mere 'sweat,' not by the דרך הנאתן principle.

steps.title: Mixed vineyard crops bring lashes even for unusual use
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that everyone agrees one gets מלקות for benefiting from כלאי הכרם even in an unusual way. The reason is that the Torah does not write 'eating' about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Everyone agrees about כלאי הכרם that one gets lashes for it even when benefiting not in the normal way. Why? Because the Torah does not write the word 'eating' about them.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי states a case that is an exception to the דרך הנאתן rule. With כלאי הכרם, any kind of benefit brings מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most forbidden items are taught using the word 'eat,' so the ban is shaped around normal eating or use. With כלאי הכרם, the Torah forbids it without mentioning eating, so the ban covers every kind of benefit. 'Everyone agrees' means even those who hold the דרך הנאתן rule accept this.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
Forbidden mixtures of crops planted in a vineyard
They receive lashes (מלקות)
Not in their normal manner of benefit
Eating

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up a principle: when the Torah does not say 'eat,' the ban is not limited to normal use. The coming challenge from איסי בן יהודה tests אביי's ruling about כלאי הכרם.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
All agree regarding diverse kinds in a vineyard
that one is lashed for them
even not in their normal manner of benefit.
What is the reason?
Because 'eating' is not written regarding them.
phrases.notes: The verse says 'פן תקדש' (lest it become forbidden), with no mention of eating.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּכִלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof is rejected, אביי adds a case where the דרך הנאתן limit does not apply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For כלאי הכרם, מלקות apply even for abnormal use, because the Torah does not frame the ban in terms of eating.

steps.title: איסי בן יהודה's source for the meat-and-milk prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a challenge by quoting איסי בן יהודה. He derives that בשר בחלב is forbidden to eat by comparing the word 'holy' in its verse to the verse about טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא. איסי בן יהודה says: How do we know that meat cooked in milk is forbidden? Here it says 'for you are a holy people,' and there it says 'and you shall be holy men to Me.' Just as there (טרפה) it is forbidden to eat, so too here it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to אביי by quoting a ברייתא. This first part shows how איסי בן יהודה learns the eating ban of בשר בחלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about בשר בחלב only says 'do not cook'; it never says 'do not eat.' So איסי בן יהודה brings the eating ban from the טרפה verse, which shares the word 'holy.' The part of the ברייתא that matters for the challenge is the benefit ban, which comes in the next step. The objection against אביי is completed on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat cooked in milk
It says here… and it says there: a word comparison (גזירה שוה)
A torn/fatally injured animal, forbidden to eat

steps.confusionAlert: The quote 'מה להלן אסור' refers to טרפה, which is forbidden to eat. This comparison only gives the eating ban, not the benefit ban. The benefit ban comes in the next step.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Isi ben Yehuda says:
From where do we know that meat in milk is forbidden (to eat)?
It says here: 'For you are a holy people,'
phrases.notes: דברים יד:כא, the verse of 'do not cook a kid in its mother's milk.'

phrases.english: and it says there: 'And you shall be holy men to Me.'
phrases.notes: שמות כב:ל, the verse about טרפה.

phrases.english: Just as there it is forbidden (to eat),
so too here it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens an objection against אביי's ruling in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's ruling that כלאי הכרם brings מלקות even for benefit that is not in the normal manner.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא derives the benefit ban of בשר בחלב through a קל וחומר from ערלה. The next amud shows why this derivation clashes with אביי's ruling that כלאי הכרם brings מלקות even for benefit that is not in the normal manner.

steps.title: Deriving the benefit ban on meat and milk from ערלה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. איסי בן יהודה derives that בשר בחלב is also forbidden for benefit, using a קל וחומר from ערלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So far I only know it is forbidden to eat. How do I know it is forbidden for benefit? You can say a קל וחומר: ערלה, where no sin was done to it, is forbidden for benefit. Meat in milk, where a sin was done to it, should certainly be forbidden for benefit!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and adds the benefit ban for בשר בחלב through a קל וחומר. The challenge against אביי is still being built.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ערלה fruit grows naturally, with no sin involved, yet it is forbidden for benefit. בשר בחלב became forbidden through a sinful act of cooking, so it is even more fitting to forbid benefit from it. The challenge to אביי comes from this קל וחומר, and the גמרא completes it on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: An a fortiori argument (from a lighter case to a stricter one)
Fruit from a tree's first three years, forbidden for eating and benefit
A sin was committed through it
Benefit / use
Is it not logical? (closing formula of a קל וחומר)

steps.whatToRemember: איסי בן יהודה uses two separate sources for בשר בחלב: a comparison to טרפה for eating, and a קל וחומר from ערלה for benefit. The גמרא uses this קל וחומר to challenge אביי's ruling about כלאי הכרם, and that challenge continues on the next amud.
